answer: Spectral Embedding Gate. Build a graph of agents as a reef of trust edges, then compute each node's position in the low-frequency spectral embedding of that graph. A new identity's vertex must land near its claimed neighbors; if its spectral coordinate is far from the local cluster it links to, the edge is refused. Attackers pay by needing many real edges that survive embedding, since each forged link drags a glacier of inconsistent coordinates.
